name: Israel
headline: Israel: +3.5% growth in 2025, 3.0% inflation, debt 68% of GDP
sections: Israel is a $617 billion economy (2025), the world's 27th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.5% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $60K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 11.2% of GDP (2024).
Consumer prices rose 3.0% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 4.4% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.0% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 6.0% (2025).
Gross government debt is 68% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 71% in 2020. The general government balance is −5.2% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +2.1% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 53% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 4.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 73% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 83.2 years (2024). Population: 10.1 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
